cases.name: R.G. Anand v. Deluxe Films
cases.facts: The dispute concerned alleged copying of a dramatic work into a film.
cases.issue: What test determines substantial copyright infringement of an idea or expression.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Copyright protects expression, not ideas, and infringement depends on substantial similarity assessed from the work as a whole.
cases.holding: The Court stated the governing comparison test.
cases.relevance: Use for copyright infringement and idea-expression distinction.

cases.name: Novartis AG v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court considered patentability of a pharmaceutical form under s. 3(d).
cases.issue: What enhanced efficacy threshold applies to a pharmaceutical derivative.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 3(d) requires the statutory enhanced-efficacy threshold and prevents evergreening without the required proof.
cases.holding: The patent claim was rejected under the statutory standard.
cases.relevance: Use for patentability exclusions and pharmaceutical patents.

cases.name: Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
cases.facts: The parties used similar marks for pharmaceutical products.
cases.issue: How should deceptive similarity be assessed in pharmaceutical trademark disputes.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must apply a stricter likelihood-of-confusion test for medicines because confusion may endanger public health.
cases.holding: The Court directed a careful comparison of the marks and circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for trademark confusion and public-interest analysis.
